content.title: Acute Heart Failure — Selected Page Extract
content.prehospital_management: Oxygen therapy may be given based on clinical judgment unless oxygen saturation is <90% in which case it should be administered. In patients with respiratory distress (respiratory rate >25 breaths/min) and oxygen saturation <90%, non-invasive ventilation should be initiated. Although therapeutic tools may be available in the prehospital setting, whether more effective prehospital care alters clinical outcome remains to be proven in randomized trials. Pre-hospital management should not delay rapid transfer of AHF patients to the most appropriate medical setting.
content.in_hospital_management: Diagnostic workup and appropriate pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment must be started promptly and in parallel. AHF patients are triaged according to degree of haemodynamic instability and illness severity. Type and intensity of monitoring depend on clinical severity, care setting and in-hospital course. Management starts with the search for specific causes of AHF (for example: ACS, hypertensive emergency, rapid arrhythmias or severe bradycardia/conduction disturbance, acute mechanical causes such as acute valve regurgitation or acute pulmonary embolism, infection including myocarditis, and tamponade [CHAMPIT]). After exclusion of these urgent causes, management differs according to clinical presentation.
content.pre_discharge_phase: Details on this phase are referenced to section 11.3.11 of the guideline.
content.notes: References and supplementary materials (Supplementary text 11.2, Supplementary Tables 17a/17b, Supplementary text 11.3) are cited for disposition decisions, monitoring details, and management algorithms. Figures referenced include Figure 12 and Figures 7 and 10 for presentation-based management pathways.
